newsitem.title: MEXICO: Canada steel chief warns Mexico exporters on US.
newsitem.headline: Canada steel chief warns Mexico exporters on US.

text.p: The chairman of Canada's Stelco Inc warned Mexican exporters Tuesday of possible protectionist moves from the United States because of soaring Mexican steel sales there.

"I would suggest that the protectionist tendencies (of the United States) should worry to a great degree those Mexican producers because of the vital role that exports markets must take in the development and expansion of their own industrial base," Fred H. Telmer told a Latin American Steel Congress here in northern Mexico.

Mexico's steel exports soared last year as producers sought new markets in the wake of the economic recession in Mexico which made national steel sales and consumption drop dramatically. Export receipts jumped to $2.769 billion in 1995 from $1.099 billion in 1994.
Telmer said Mexican steel exports have soared again in 1996, up 22.8 percent in the first seven months of the year.

"Given that the destiny of the majority of these exports is the United States...in the short term they could turn out to be a big problem and threat in the eyes of U.S. trade regulatory authorities," he added.

He said Canada knew all too well the rigour with which the United States applies trade laws. "I have the scars to prove it," he added refering to past disputes with U.S. authorities and steel companies.

Telmer said if the spirit of the North American Free Trade Agreement was to shine through at the end of the day the senselessness of companies slapping anti-dumping suits against each other had to end. "The obvious priority is the development of a mechanism that allows a clear differentiation between lawful and unlawful import practices," he concluded.
